primitives.name: Transient Ice Conduction Profile
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Heat equation ∂u/∂t = α_I ∂2u/∂x2 on 0<x<30 mm with u(0,t)=T_S(t), u(L,t)=T_I(t).
primitives.latex: \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha_I \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}, \quad 0 < x < L
primitives.assumptions: One-dimensional heat conduction, constant thermal diffusivity, Dirichlet boundary conditions known from measurement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When boundary conditions deviate significantly from fitted polynomials or when non-linear effects dominate.

primitives.name: Eigenfunction Series Solution

primitives.latex: u(x,t) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \left[ \int_0^t e^{-\alpha \lambda_n^2 (t-\tau)} \hat{S}_n(\tau) d\tau + e^{-\alpha \lambda_n^2 t} c_n \right] \sin(\lambda_n x), \quad \lambda_n = \frac{n\pi}{L}

This setup allows for an analytical solution via eigenfunction expansion, which is derived using separation of variables and Fourier series. The resulting expression captures how temperature evolves within the ice slab over time, conditioned on known surface temperatures. The utility lies in its ability to predict thermal gradients without resorting to computationally expensive numerical simulations. However, the solution remains conditional on accurate measurement of boundary conditions—specifically, the surface temperature history—which limits its direct applicability to real-time prediction engines unless those conditions are externally provided. The model assumes constant thermal properties and one-dimensionality, both of which may fail under complex environmental or operational scenarios. Thus, while the primitive provides a robust kernel for simulating ice behavior, it lacks autonomy for independent inference without external calibration data.
